howToPlay.title: How to play
howToPlay.intro: Sea Battle is a guessing duel. Both fleets are hidden; you find the enemy ships one shot at a time. If you have not played in years, these four steps are the whole game.

goal.title: The goal
goal.body: Sink all ten enemy ships before the opponent sinks yours. You never see where their fleet is — only what your own shots reveal.

place.title: Place your fleet
place.board: The board is a 10 x 10 grid, columns A to J and rows 1 to 10. You place ten ships covering twenty squares in total:
place.orientation: Every ship sits in a straight line, either horizontally or vertically — never diagonally — and must fit completely on the board. Drag a ship onto the grid, or select it and tap a square. Press R or use the Rotate button to switch between horizontal and vertical. Auto-place fills the whole board for you.
place.fleetDiagram: The ten ships of a fleet: one four-square ship, two of three squares, three of two squares and four single squares.

touching.title: Keep your ships apart
touching.body: Ships may not touch each other. There must be at least one clear square between any two ships.
touching.diagonals: This includes corners: two ships that meet only diagonally are still touching, and the placement is rejected.
touching.help: You do not have to count squares yourself. The preview turns red and the board shakes when a position is illegal, so you can only ever place a legal fleet.
touching.legalDiagram: Two ships separated by one clear row — a legal placement.
touching.illegalDiagram: Two ships meeting at a corner — rejected, because diagonal contact still counts as touching.

fire.title: Take turns firing
fire.turns: You fire first. On your turn you pick one square on the enemy grid and fire a single shot. A shot is either a miss, a hit, or the hit that sinks a ship.
fire.againLead: A hit earns you another shot.
fire.again: Keep firing as long as you keep hitting. The turn passes to your opponent only when you miss.
fire.noRepeat: You cannot fire at the same square twice — squares you have already resolved are not selectable.
fire.outcomesDiagram: Firing grid marks: a hollow ring for a miss, an orange burst for a hit, and a crossed red block for part of a sunk ship.

sink.title: Sink the fleet
sink.body: When every square of a ship has been hit, the ship sinks and its full outline is revealed.
sink.buffer: Because ships can never touch, every square around a sunk ship is guaranteed to be empty water. Those squares are marked for you automatically with small dots, and you cannot waste a shot on them.
sink.win: The first player to sink all ten of the opponent's ships wins immediately.
sink.bufferDiagram: A sunk two-square ship surrounded by dots marking the squares that are now known to be empty.

easy.name: Easy
easy.body: Fires at random squares. A relaxed warm-up while you get the feel of the board.

medium.name: Medium
medium.body: Searches in a pattern, and once it lands a hit it works along the ship until it sinks it.

hard.name: Hard
hard.body: Works out which squares your remaining ships could still occupy and fires where a ship is most likely to be. A genuinely tough opponent.

salvo.title: Salvo mode
salvo.body: A faster variant is planned: instead of one shot per turn, you fire a salvo of as many shots as you have surviving ships, choosing every target before any of them is resolved. The turn always passes afterwards — in Salvo a hit does not earn another go. Today SeaDuel plays the Classic rules described above.

faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.intro: Short answers about what SeaDuel does today.

registration.a: No. There is no sign-up at all — open the page and play. Accounts are planned for a later stage so that results can be kept, but nothing is gated behind one today.

free.a: Yes. SeaDuel is free to play, there are no adverts, and no feature is locked behind a payment.

bot.a: A computer opponent, at Easy, Medium or Hard. The bot plays by exactly the same rules you do and only sees what you would see of your board — it cannot look at your ship positions.

friend.q: Can I play against a friend?
friend.a: Not yet. At the moment SeaDuel is a single-player game against the bot. Playing another person is planned but not built.

mobile.q: Does it work on my phone?
mobile.a: Yes. SeaDuel runs in the browser on phones, tablets and desktops, and there is nothing to install. On a touchscreen you can drag a ship onto the grid or tap to place it, and tap a square to fire.

rating.q: Is there a rating or a leaderboard?
rating.a: Not yet. Games against the bot are practice only and are not scored or ranked.

data.q: What do you store about me?
data.a: Because there are no accounts, there is no profile to create or delete. Your browser remembers two things locally: the language you chose and whether sound is muted. Clearing your browser data removes both.
